correctness.rationale: A maximal independent subset on C_n has cyclic selected gap lengths exactly 2 or 3. Independent continuous uniform arrival marks yield conditional factors A(s,t)=1−min(s,t) for a gap 2 and B(s,t)=(1−s)(1−t) for a gap 3; integrate their product over selected marks. On a common six-edge arc, replacing 222 by 33 leads G(s,t)=∫∫A(s,x)A(x,y)A(y,t)dxdy≥(2/3)(1−s)(1−t)=2H(s,t) where H=(1−s)(1−t)/3; an exterior factor is common and nonnegative. For n=6 endpoints coincide and the same bound holds; for every n≥8 the remaining n−6 is a sum of 2/3 gaps. For n=3,4,5,7 maximal gap profiles lie in one rotation orbit. Consequently uniform iff n∈{3,4,5,7}, all other n carry a ≥2 positive probability ratio. Independently re-derived exact rational first-accepted-vertex laws for n=3..11: C6 has output weights 1/9 and 1/3; C7 uniform 1/7; C8 min1/15 vs max7/30; this is corroborative of universal integral proof.

value.rationale: Uniformity of random-order greedy maximal independent sets is a natural algorithmic sampling question. The exact four exceptional cycle lengths and explicit six-edge local likelihood-ratio obstruction give a sharp structural boundary, rather than generic well-coveredness or just expected set size. The pointwise factor-two witness persists for all large cycles and is a useful sampling-bias diagnostic.

limitations: Only uniform random vertex-order greedy maximal independent sets in labelled simple cycles C_n,n≥3.
